First, compute a "Self-Containment Ratio" for each borough, using exactly this method:
1. Departures = number of trips that started in that borough
2. Self-contained trips = number of those departures that also ended in the same borough
3. Self-Containment Ratio = Self-contained trips / Departures

Now, using the borough adjacency list, identify specific individual boroughs (not an overall city-wide pattern) that fall into one of these two categories:
- HOT SPOT: a borough with a high Self-Containment Ratio that is ALSO surrounded by other high-Self-Containment Ratio neighboring boroughs
- COLD SPOT: a borough with a low Self-Containment Ratio that is ALSO surrounded by other low-Self-Containment Ratio neighboring boroughs

If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

Thought: Compute Self-Containment Ratio (SCR) for each StartBorough.  
Action:

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load trips data
DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/cyclehire_w007.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)

# Compute departures and self-contained trips per borough
departures = df.groupby("StartBorough")["Rental Id"].count().rename("departures")
self_contained = df[df["StartBorough"] == df["EndBorough"]].groupby("StartBorough")["Rental Id"].count().rename("self_contained")

# Combine into DataFrame
scr = pd.concat([departures, self_contained], axis=1).fillna(0)
scr["SCR"] = scr["self_contained"] / scr["departures"]
scr = scr.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "borough"})
print(scr.sort_values("SCR", ascending=False))
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load SCR data
DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/cyclehire_w007.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
departures = df.groupby("StartBorough")["Rental Id"].count().rename("departures")
self_contained = df[df["StartBorough"] == df["EndBorough"]].groupby("StartBorough")["Rental Id"].count().rename("self_contained")
scr = pd.concat([departures, self_contained], axis=1).fillna(0)
scr["SCR"] = scr["self_contained"] / scr["departures"]
scr = scr.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "borough"})

# Load adjacency
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Merge SCR values for neighbors
adj = adj.merge(scr[["borough","SCR"]], left_on="neighbor", right_on="borough", how="left")
adj = adj.rename(columns={"SCR":"neighbor_SCR"}).drop(columns=["borough_y"])
adj = adj.rename(columns={"borough_x":"borough"})
# Compute neighbor average SCR
nbr_avg = adj.groupby("borough")["neighbor_SCR"].mean().rename("nbr_avg_SCR").reset_index()
scr = scr.merge(nbr_avg, on="borough", how="left")

# Compute global mean SCR
global_mean = scr["SCR"].mean()
print("Global mean SCR:", global_mean)

# Identify hot and cold spots
hot = scr[(scr["SCR"] > global_mean) & (scr["nbr_avg_SCR"] > global_mean)]
cold = scr[(scr["SCR"] < global_mean) & (scr["nbr_avg_SCR"] < global_mean)]

print("Hot candidates:\n", hot[["borough","SCR","nbr_avg_SCR"]])
print("Cold candidates:\n", cold[["borough","SCR","nbr_avg_SCR"]])
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load trips data
DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/cyclehire_w007.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)

# Calculate departures per borough
departures = df.groupby("StartBorough").size().rename("departures").reset_index()

# Calculate self-contained trips per borough
self_ct = df[df["StartBorough"] == df["EndBorough"]].groupby("StartBorough").size().rename("self_contained").reset_index()

# Combine
scr = departures.merge(self_ct, on="StartBorough", how="left").fillna({"self_contained":0})
scr["SCR"] = scr["self_contained"] / scr["departures"]
scr = scr.rename(columns={"StartBorough":"borough"})
print("SCR per borough:\n", scr[["borough","SCR"]])

# Load adjacency
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
print("Adjacency sample:\n", adj.head())

# Merge to get neighbor SCR
adj2 = adj.merge(scr[["borough","SCR"]], left_on="neighbor", right_on="borough", how="left")
adj2 = adj2.rename(columns={"SCR":"neighbor_SCR"}).drop(columns=["borough"])
# Compute neighbor average SCR
nbr_avg = adj2.groupby("borough")["neighbor_SCR"].mean().reset_index().rename(columns={"neighbor_SCR":"nbr_avg_SCR"})
scr = scr.merge(nbr_avg, on="borough", how="left")
print("SCR with neighbor avg:\n", scr)

# Global mean SCR
global_mean = scr["SCR"].mean()
print("Global mean SCR:", global_mean)

# Identify hot and cold spots
hot = scr[(scr["SCR"] > global_mean) & (scr["nbr_avg_SCR"] > global_mean)]
cold = scr[(scr["SCR"] < global_mean) & (scr["nbr_avg_SCR"] < global_mean)]

print("Hot spot candidates:\n", hot[["borough","SCR","nbr_avg_SCR"]])
print("Cold spot candidates:\n", cold[["borough","SCR","nbr_avg_SCR"]])
```
